our_argument_summary: WIN-025 verdict Std Model Explains. Eclipse-induced ±10 nT geomagnetic variations are predicted by Chapman-Sq ionospheric framework (Chapman 1919; Yamazaki & Maute 2017; Kim & Chang 2018). The dome derives a station-to-station scaling FSF = H(r)/r that reproduces the 9-station Pearson r ≈ 0.9999 fit; the absolute magnitude baseline is imported from the 2017 Boulder single-station observation. WIN-025 detail_extra credits the dome author 2026-03-15 voluntary removal as self-correction while showing the stated rationale (Kp ~5–6) is contradicted by the GFZ Potsdam record (eclipse-hour Kp 0.0–1.3, peak across April 7–9 = 3.3). Post-EXP-244 citation cluster canonicalized (Chapman 1933→1919 residuals cleared; Chapman 1919 appears 3× in current WIN-025 vs 6× at c7 audit — schema stable, no drift).

dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: FSF station-to-station ratio: c7 characterized this as "genuinely computed from dome parameters (firmament height H(r) divided by station dome-coordinate r)". This characterization is now SUPERSEDED by EXP-624 (WIN-010-c11-c12-six-hole-batch, ISS-2746 patches P3+P6): V12 (r·tan(θ) = H(r)) forces H(r)/r = tan(θ) at every station, so FSF_i = tan(lat_i)/tan(lat_BOU) regardless of the interpolating H(r) family. FSF is provably H(r)-independent; the exponential H(r) = 8537·exp(-r/8619) is mathematically inert in the FSF calculation. WIN-025 has NOT been patched to reflect this — it still credits FSF as a genuine dome-geometric derivation.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Chapman-Sq ionospheric framework (Chapman 1919; Yamazaki & Maute 2017) predicts eclipse-induced ±10 nT surface variations. Chernogor & Holub themselves attribute the observed effect to ionospheric conductivity changes, not aether.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: Sq perturbations of 5–30 nT described since 1919; quantitatively verified in Kim & Chang 2018 39-eclipse ensemble. v31→v45 evolution log (raw-text/06-evolution.txt lines 18–21) explicitly says v31 predicted 2024 eclipse magnitudes identically across all latitudes and the FSF formula was introduced at v45 to fit the same 9-station dataset that became WIN-025.

Even the relative scaling is not a dome-geometric derivation; it is a trigonometric identity of geographic latitude that any smooth H(r) satisfying V12 produces identically. Tag value derives_from_dome=false stands but the EVIDENCE string in WIN-025 is stale. WIN-025 should carry the V12 reduction the way WIN-010 does.

holes_found.description: CROSS-WIN INCONSISTENCY POST-EXP-624. WIN-010 detail_evidence (post-2026-06-16 EXP-624 P3+P6 patches, ISS-2746 close) now proves algebraically that FSF = H(r)/r reduces to tan(lat_i)/tan(lat_BOU) via V12 — the exponential H(r) is mathematically inert; FSF is a pure trigonometric identity on geographic latitude that any smooth H(r) satisfying V12 produces identically. WIN-010 evidence contains this in explicit form (12 mentions of V12, 12 mentions of tan(lat), the exact phrase "provably H(r)-independent" appears once). WIN-025 evidence contains ZERO mentions of V12, tan(lat), trigonometric, algebraically, or H(r)-independent — it still credits FSF as "a real dome-geometric derivation that reproduces the 9-station Pearson r ≈ 0.9999 fit" (detail_evidence sentence) and "the FSF = H(r)/r station-to-station ratio is a genuine geometric derivation from dome parameters" (detail_verdict_text sentence). A dome defender reading the WIN-010/025/068 cluster side-by-side can now compile a legitimate self-contradiction attack: "You say in WIN-025 that FSF is a genuine dome-geometric derivation. You say in WIN-010 that the same FSF is H(r)-independent and equals tan(lat) regardless of H. These cannot both be true. Which one is your position?" This is the exact reader-path attack surface concern from the holistic-check menu. Cross-WIN consistency is now broken on the cluster's most-central technical claim. Recommendation: patch WIN-025 finding + detail_evidence + detail_verdict_text to reflect the V12 reduction, either by (a) explicitly citing WIN-010's algebraic result and softening the "genuine geometric derivation" language to "reduces algebraically to tan(lat) via V12 — see WIN-010 for the derivation," or (b) importing an abbreviated version of EXP-624 patches P3+P6 into WIN-025 directly. Path (a) is simpler and centralizes the algebraic argument on WIN-010 where it currently lives. This is the highest-value patch remaining on WIN-025.
holes_found.recommendation: Open ISS on WIN-025 to align the FSF characterization with WIN-010 post-EXP-624. Prefer path (a): a 2–3 sentence edit in WIN-025 detail_verdict_text noting that FSF reduces to tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) via V12 (H(r)-independent) with cross-reference to WIN-010. Same edit should apply to WIN-068 as a follow-up (WIN-068 correctly notes FSF is a spectator for the 39-eclipse ensemble but does not carry the V12 reduction either).

stronger_arguments.description: The V12 reduction IS the strongest kill-shot on the FSF-derivation claim, and WIN-025 is the natural home for it because WIN-025 is the WIN whose scoreboard entry ("CONFIRMED ~-10 nT across 9 stations") is anchored on the station-to-station scaling that FSF is supposed to explain. Currently the algebraic result lives only in WIN-010 (BOU 2017 single-station). Moving or mirroring the V12 argument into WIN-025 (9-station) increases its retrievability for a reader who lands on WIN-025 directly and doubles the reader-path attack surface coverage. Companion opportunity in the walkthrough: §11 thesis-challenge cluster and Part 2b code-analysis discussion of derives_from_dome=false should reference the V12 reduction with WIN-025 as the primary worked example (9 stations is more visually decisive than 1).

The dual-baseline (BOU/W004) pre-registration attack surface has landed in WIN-010 (BOU/W004 ratio = 0.4901 verified across all 9 stations to ±0.5%) but is not mirrored in WIN-025. WIN-025 is the WIN that would be adjudicated by the 2026-08-12 European eclipse observations, so the pre-registration argument (dome must specify which baseline path applies at each station before 2026-08-12 to avoid pick-after-the-fact) belongs on WIN-025's detail_verdict_text as much as on WIN-010's. Currently only WIN-010 carries the dual-baseline pre-registration language.

kernel_of_truth.description: Three pieces of genuine content on WIN-025 as of HEAD c80f1ca: (1) The observation is real — Chernogor & Holub (2024, Adv. Space Res., DOI 10.1016/j.asr.2024.10.056) documented ±10 nT variations at 9 INTERMAGNET stations during April 8, 2024 eclipse under quiet Kp 0.0–1.3 (data/wins.json WIN-025 detail_evidence:para1). (2) The dome correctly notes the magnetic signal tracks eclipse geometry rather than solar noon — this observable is non-trivial in the sense that a strict solar-noon-locked mechanism would not produce it (data/wins.json WIN-025 detail_evidence:para3). (3) The 2026-03-15 voluntary WIN-025 removal is genuine self-correction in process even though the stated Kp ~5–6 premise is factually wrong per the GFZ record (data/wins.json WIN-025 detail_extra:para2). All three survive the V12 reduction unchanged.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The V12 reduction converts a partial defense into an active prosecution across all three kernels: (1) the observation being real is co-predicted by Chapman-Sq physics (raw-text/06-evolution.txt v31 admission plus Chapman 1919 canonical framework), so "real observation" is not discriminating; (2) the eclipse-geometry-tracking observable falls out of Sq physics by construction (moon shadow reduces conductivity where the shadow physically moves through the ionosphere), so both models predict this — non-discriminating; (3) self-correction on a false premise is process-virtuous but does not retroactively make the original prediction prospective, and the v31→v45 patch history (raw-text/06-evolution.txt lines 18–21) shows the eclipse-specific FSF formula was introduced at v45 to fit the same 9-station dataset that became the WIN. The V12 result adds a fourth prosecution vector new to this spot-check: even after conceding FSF as station-to-station scaling, the scaling itself is H(r)-independent tan(lat) trigonometry (monitor/analyst/expansions/EXP-624 patches P3+P6) — the dome derives no dome-specific physics, not even the relative scaling. The published FSF table is a tan(latitude) ratio reproducible from geographic latitudes alone; the exponential H(r) = 8537·exp(-r/8619) is mathematically inert (data/wins.json WIN-010 detail_evidence). Every dome-adjacent element of the WIN-025 claim is now downstream of either an imported observation or a trigonometric identity — nothing left is derived from firmament height, aetheric medium properties, or firmament conductivity.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A charitable dome defender who has read the review's six methodological principles would attack WIN-025 with a two-move sequence. Move 1 (self-contradiction pincer): "Your own WIN-025 concedes FSF = H(r)/r is a genuine geometric derivation from dome parameters (detail_verdict_text). Your WIN-010 asserts the same FSF is provably H(r)-independent and equals tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) regardless of H(r). Both cannot be true. Under your own "internal consistency first" principle, one of these WINs is wrong. Which one — and once you retract it, does the retraction unwind the other WIN in the cluster?" This is a legitimate attack that we manufactured ourselves by landing EXP-624 on WIN-010 without mirroring to WIN-025/WIN-068. Move 2 (concession leveraging): "WIN-025 detail_verdict_text concedes 'FSF = H(r)/r station-to-station ratio is a genuine geometric derivation from dome parameters (Pearson r ≈ 0.9999, verified independently in the WIN-010/WIN-068 cluster)'. Even taking your V12 result at face value, WIN-025's own text is signed evidence that we DID derive the station scaling from dome parameters. You are asking us to defer to a WIN-010 analysis that overturns your own WIN-025 concession. That is the definition of goalpost-moving after we passed the original test." This second move is weaker because the V12 result is mathematically decisive (any smooth H(r) satisfying V12 produces the same FSF), but it forces us to explain the ordering of concession-then-retraction across two WINs that share a cluster.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Patch WIN-025 to align with WIN-010 immediately — see hole #1 recommendation. When the patch lands, also add one sentence to WIN-010 detail_evidence noting that the V12 reduction applies uniformly across the WIN-010/025/068 cluster (rather than being specific to BOU 2017) so a defender reading only WIN-010 cannot argue it is a WIN-specific artifact. Alignment across the cluster closes the pincer.

deeper_analysis:
This spot-check was selected because WIN-025 last received a full-detail review 73 days ago (c7, 2026-04-25) — the OLDEST most-recent reviewed_at across the 70 reviewed WINs. In the intervening 10 weeks the cluster underwent one major EXP: EXP-624 (2026-06-16 batch on WIN-010, six patches, ISS-2746 among others). EXP-624 landed the algebraic V12 tan(lat) reduction result on WIN-010 without mirroring the same result onto WIN-025 or WIN-068. The result is a cross-WIN inconsistency where WIN-025 concedes FSF is genuine dome geometry while WIN-010 proves it is not. From a dome-defender adversarial standpoint this is a live attack surface — the two WINs are cross-referenced within the cluster and any reader who samples both will see them saying opposite things about the single most-central technical claim (whether the dome derives ANYTHING from its geometry in the 9-station eclipse scoreboard entry).

The fix is not architecturally hard: the algebraic argument lives in EXP-624 patches P3+P6 in a form roughly 400 words long, and adding a 2–3 sentence pointer to WIN-025 ("FSF reduces algebraically to tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) via V12 — see WIN-010 for derivation") closes the inconsistency without duplicating the derivation. The value/effort ratio is high; the fix is a small ISS-scoped edit.

All other c7 findings remain in the state c7 predicted: EXP-244 citation canonicalization closed cleanly (Chapman 1933 count = 0 in current wins.json; Chapman 1919 anchor consistent across the cluster); FAIL-007 cross-page alignment (c7 H3 / ISS-1514) is not visible in current uncounted-failures.json but likely closed in the intervening period; ISS-1508 (tldr_verdict "2017 observation" self-containment) is still visible in current text but marked closed 2026-04-24 in closed-issues.json — this is a possible ledger-vs-content discrepancy flagged for further tracing but non-blocking for verdict.

Overall assessment: WIN-025 verdict Std Model Explains stands unchanged. The V12 reduction strengthens the derives_from_dome=false argument by removing the last plausible "the dome derived at least the station scaling" partial defense. The recommended patch is minor_edit — align WIN-025 (and follow-up WIN-068) with the WIN-010 V12 result.
